title: Sleep

source.name: Wikipedia — Sleep
source.note: Đã rút gọn: chỉ giữ một số đoạn.

paras: Sleep is a state of reduced mental and physical activity in which consciousness is altered and certain sensory activity is inhibited. During sleep, there is a marked decrease in muscle activity and interactions with the surrounding environment. While sleep differs from wakefulness in terms of the ability to react to stimuli, it still involves active brain patterns, making it more reactive than a coma or disorders of consciousness.

Sleep occurs in repeating periods, during which the body alternates between two distinct modes: rapid eye movement sleep (REM) and non-REM sleep. Although REM stands for "rapid eye movement", this mode of sleep has many other aspects, including virtual paralysis of the body. Dreams are a succession of images, ideas, emotions, and sensations that usually occur involuntarily in the mind during certain stages of sleep.

During sleep, most of the body's systems are in an anabolic state, helping to restore the immune, nervous, skeletal, and muscular systems; these are vital processes that maintain mood, memory, and cognitive function, and play a large role in the function of the endocrine and immune systems. The internal circadian clock promotes sleep daily at night, when it is dark. However, midday naps may also be necessary: current research is studying power naps. The diverse purposes and mechanisms of sleep are the subject of substantial ongoing research. Sleep is a highly conserved behavior across animal evolution, likely going back hundreds of millions of years, and originating as a means for the brain to cleanse itself of waste products. Researchers have found that cleansing, including the removal of amyloid, may be a core purpose of sleep.

Humans may suffer from various sleep disorders, including dyssomnias, such as insomnia, hypersomnia, narcolepsy, and sleep apnea; parasomnias, such as sleepwalking and rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder; bruxism; and circadian rhythm sleep disorders. The use of artificial light has substantially altered humanity's sleep patterns. Common sources of artificial light include outdoor lighting and the screens of digital devices such as smartphones and televisions, which emit large amounts of blue light, a form of light typically associated with daytime. This disrupts the release of the hormone melatonin needed to regulate the sleep cycle.

Sleep is divided into two broad types: non-rapid eye movement (non-REM or NREM) sleep and rapid eye movement (REM) sleep. Non-REM and REM sleep are so different that physiologists identify them as distinct behavioral states. Non-REM sleep occurs first and after a transitional period is called slow-wave sleep or deep sleep. During this phase, body temperature and heart rate fall, and the brain uses less energy. REM sleep, also known as paradoxical sleep, represents a smaller portion of total sleep time. It is the main occasion for dreams (or nightmares), and is associated with desynchronized and fast brain waves, eye movements, loss of muscle tone, and suspension of homeostasis.

questions.q: How does sleep differ from a coma, according to paragraph 1?
options: The sleeping person never changes between one state and another
The sleeping brain stops all activity until the person wakes up
The sleeping brain is still active and can respond more readily
The sleeping body can react to every kind of sound or movement
questions.explain: Đoạn 1: giấc ngủ vẫn “involves active brain patterns, making it more reactive than a coma”.

questions.q: What does the text suggest about the origin of sleep?
options: It began when animals first needed to avoid hunting during the night hours
It developed only in humans after the arrival of artificial lighting
It may have begun as a way of clearing waste from the brain
It was invented by animals that live in very cold regions of the world
questions.explain: Đoạn 3: giấc ngủ có từ hàng trăm triệu năm, “originating as a means for the brain to cleanse itself of waste products”.

questions.q: What does the writer imply with the words “may be a core purpose of sleep”?
options: Researchers have stopped studying the purposes of sleep
Researchers are not yet certain that this cleansing is a main function
Researchers have proved that this cleansing is the only function
Researchers believe that this cleansing is unimportant for health
questions.explain: Đoạn 3: cách nói “may be” thể hiện sự dè dặt – việc dọn rác của não có thể là chức năng cốt lõi nhưng chưa được khẳng định.

questions.q: Why might using a smartphone late at night affect a person’s sleep?
options: Its battery produces heat that raises the temperature of the body
Its screen emits blue light that disturbs a hormone controlling sleep
Its sound keeps the brain in a state of slow-wave sleep
Its signal prevents the body from entering a state of REM sleep
questions.explain: Đoạn 4: màn hình phát nhiều ánh sáng xanh – thường gắn với ban ngày – làm gián đoạn việc tiết melatonin cần thiết để điều hòa chu kỳ ngủ.

options: The person is aware of the room and can easily be woken
The eyes move quickly and the muscles are very active
The body temperature rises and the brain works at full speed
The body cools, the pulse slows and the brain needs less energy
questions.explain: Đoạn 5: giai đoạn ngủ sâu “body temperature and heart rate fall, and the brain uses less energy”.

questions.q: How does REM sleep compare with non-REM sleep?
options: It is the type of sleep in which body temperature falls the most
It happens first and is followed by a transitional period
It takes up most of the night and has no connection with dreams
It takes up a smaller share of the night and is when most dreaming happens
questions.explain: Đoạn 5: REM “represents a smaller portion of total sleep time. It is the main occasion for dreams”; non-REM xảy ra trước.

questions.q: The body’s internal clock tends to make people sleepy during the night.
questions.explain: Đoạn 3: “The internal circadian clock promotes sleep daily at night, when it is dark.”

questions.q: Most adults need between seven and nine hours of sleep each night.
questions.explain: Bài không nêu số giờ ngủ cần thiết.
